sources.title: Grok 4.1 Fast and Agent Tools API, November 19, 2025
sources.evidence: Dated launch explicitly releases the reasoning and non-reasoning Fast API variants. Describes long-horizon reinforcement learning and tool use, with 2M context; gives no parameter or network-topology disclosure.
sources.parameter_reaudit_evidence: Fresh original launch reopened and HTTP 200 retrieved October 27. Read RL training, long-horizon training, comparison tables and the exact reasoning/non-reasoning variant list. It discloses no nominal total or active size and no counted named base. Agent Tools API infrastructure is separate from the model being assessed.

sources.title: November 19, 2025 API release notes
sources.evidence: Confirms Grok 4.1 Fast available in the enterprise API on November 19. This is distinct from the November 17 consumer Grok 4.1 release.

sources.title: Grok 4.1 Fast historical provider specifications
sources.evidence: Exact xai.grok-4-1-fast-reasoning row generates thinking tokens; key specifications list text/image inputs, text output, 2,000,000 context and function calling. One introductory sentence omits 4.1, but title and exact identifiers consistently name 4.1 Fast.
sources.parameter_reaudit_evidence: Fresh original provider page reopened and HTTP 200 retrieved. Intro explicitly says Grok 4.1 Fast improves upon Grok 4 Fast primarily through specialized agentic training; exact reasoning row generates thinking tokens. Neither target nor predecessor count is provided. Model Parameters describes API sampling controls, not learned weights.

sources.title: May 15, 2026 model retirement
sources.evidence: Retires original grok-4-1-fast-reasoning on May 15, 2026 and redirects its slug to Grok 4.3 with low reasoning effort. Replacement specifications do not describe the original Fast release.

sources.title: Former exact native model documentation
sources.evidence: Direct request redirects to the current model roster. Original specifications instead rely on the retained exact launch and historical provider documentation; no current authenticated inference operation was tested.

sources.title: Former Google Cloud Grok 4.1 Fast documentation URL
sources.evidence: Parent verification found this URL redirects to the current general Grok model page. It does not presently expose the historical exact-model contract, so no Google context or availability claim is based on this route.

sources.title: Microsoft Foundry Grok 4.1 Fast Reasoning
sources.evidence: Exact model page confirms xAI authorship, text/image inputs, text output and reasoning. Its 128K context is a route-specific limit. Technical-specification and training-disclosure sections supply no parameter or neural network details.
sources.parameter_reaudit_evidence: Fresh exact-model provider page reopened and HTTP 200 retrieved. Technical specs and training disclosure contain no nominal total/active count or counted base identification.

sources.title: Launch-period enterprise terms
sources.evidence: Terms govern API service, grant limited non-transferable use, reserve xAI ownership of underlying technology, and restrict copying/reverse engineering. Supports descriptive proprietary access classification.

sources.title: xAI public checkpoint inventory
sources.evidence: Live public organization inventory contains Grok 1 and Grok 2, with no Grok 4.1 Fast checkpoint. Used with hosted distribution and service terms; older checkpoint licenses are not transferred.

sources.title: Grok 4.1 Model Card
sources.evidence: Downloaded and searched complete six-page card. It covers consumer Grok 4.1 Thinking/Non-Thinking and contains no exact Grok 4.1 Fast reference or parameter/architecture disclosure. It is not silently treated as the Fast model card.
sources.parameter_reaudit_evidence: Freshly reopened original six-page PDF; searched complete same-day cached text and read introduction and Data and Training. Standard consumer Grok 4.1 Thinking/Non-Thinking is not explicitly Fast; pretraining, midtraining and SFT/RL do not establish a counted unchanged Fast base.

sources.title: Frontier Artificial Intelligence Framework, December 2025
sources.evidence: Searched the complete later framework for exact Fast identity and size/network disclosures. Its historical training dates identify standard Grok 4.1 and Grok 4 Fast separately; no exact 4.1 Fast parameter or topology disclosure found.
sources.parameter_reaudit_evidence: Freshly reopened original eleven-page PDF and read same-day cached full text. Data Disclosure lists trillions of training tokens, not parameters, and separately names Grok 4 Fast and standard Grok 4.1. No exact 4.1 Fast total/active count.

sources.title: Grok 4.5 Model Card
sources.evidence: Searched complete later developer card and comparison tables for Grok 4.1 Fast. No exact Fast parameter or neural architecture disclosure was found; later model specifications are not transferred.
sources.parameter_reaudit_evidence: Fresh original PDF reopened; searched complete same-day cached text for exact Fast names, learned counts and active-count columns, and read section 1.2. No Fast count or counted unchanged-base relationship appears.

sources.title: Grok 4.6 Model Card
sources.evidence: Searched complete later developer card and comparison tables for Grok 4.1 Fast. No exact Fast parameter or neural architecture disclosure was found; later model specifications are not transferred.
sources.parameter_reaudit_evidence: Fresh original PDF reopened; searched complete same-day cached text and read section 1.2. Grok 4.5 generates SFT trajectories for 4.6; this is teacher-data lineage, not Fast weight identity. No Fast total/active parameter count found.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 Model Card
sources.evidence: Searched complete later developer card and comparison tables for Grok 4.1 Fast. No exact Fast parameter or neural architecture disclosure was found; later model specifications are not transferred.
sources.parameter_reaudit_evidence: Fresh original PDF reopened; searched complete same-day cached text and read section 1.2. Grok 4.6 generates SFT trajectories for 4.7; neither this training nor later comparisons establish a Fast total/active count.

sources.title: Grok 4 Fast launch and predecessor lineage
sources.evidence: Fresh original full announcement read and HTTP 200 fetched. Grok 4 Fast is described as smaller/faster and built on learnings from Grok 4, not an unchanged Grok 4 checkpoint. Its reasoning and non-reasoning modes use the same weights. No nominal total or active count is supplied, so Oracle’s named Fast training predecessor yields no transferable number.

sources.title: xAI Frontier Artificial Intelligence Framework, June 30, 2026
sources.evidence: Fresh original PDF opened and complete same-day cached text searched for total/active parameters and exact Fast identity. No learned-parameter count or named unchanged counted base for Grok 4.1 Fast is disclosed.

sources.title: OVO-S-Bench: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Streaming Spatial Intelligence in Multimodal LLMs, Tables 2, 3 and 14
sources.evidence: Fresh original research HTML read and HTTP 200 fetched. Table 2 lists unqualified Grok-4.1-Fast with a dash in Params, Table 3 compares thinking/non-thinking variants, and Table 14 explicitly names Grok-4.1-Fast-Reasoning but gives only decoding settings. No numeric learned total or active count is supplied. This later benchmark is checked for a missed size convention; its endpoint identity after the native retirement is not treated as established.

name.note: Display name for exact native API slug grok-4-1-fast-reasoning; catalog uses a dot in the version portion.

developer.note: Original developer attribution from the launch and provider model page; later corporate branding does not change release attribution.

family.note: Explicit Grok family, with Fast and reasoning designations retained.

release_date.note: Exact API variant released on this date. Earlier standard consumer Grok 4.1 and later regional provider dates are distinct. No earlier exact Fast availability was established.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is hosted API service under restricted rights; no exact public checkpoint offered in checked developer releases.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted model, supported by limited service access and retained underlying technology rights.

parameters_b.note: Fresh exact-model and later original-source review found no supported nominal total. Oracle names Grok 4 Fast as a predecessor through specialized training, but no supported count was found for that base either. Standard consumer Grok 4.1 is not explicitly the Fast base; later replacement and teacher-model counts are not transferred.

active_parameters_b.note: Separately rechecked nominal active counts and later research tables. OVO-S-Bench identifies the reasoning variant in decoding settings but supplies no active-count convention; its unqualified Fast Params cell is blank. Thinking-token budgets, API sampling controls, speed and external tools do not establish active neural parameters.

architecture.note: Exact-name training and interpretability searches and later card checks found no primary Transformer/dense/MoE topology disclosure. Reinforcement learning describes training, not network structure.

context_window.note: Original native limit is two million tokens. Microsoft Foundry documents 128K on its route, and the later Grok 4.3 redirect has a different contract.

modalities.note: Exact historical serving specifications agree on text/image input and text output. Media handled through external search or separate voice services is not native audio/video input.

reasoning.note: Explicit reasoning variant produces thinking tokens. This is a documented mode, not inferred from general problem-solving benchmarks.

tool_call.note: Exact launch and provider specifications explicitly support tool/function calling, distinct from merely using a search-enabled client.

description.value: Reasoning variant of Grok 4.1 Fast, with text and image input, tool calling and a two-million-token context window.
description.note: Factual original-variant description; avoids unsupported comparative speed or performance claims.

Also freshly opened Agentic Proposing original HTML (https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03279v1; /tmp/parameter-528-reaudit/proposing.txt), whose unqualified Fast benchmark gives no textual numeric count; it is not used to identify this reasoning variant. Secondary directory estimates were not promoted to specifications.
parameter_reaudit.lineage_review: Accepted nominal counts and explicit named-base training relationships were sought. Oracle explicitly names Grok 4 Fast and specialized training, but no supported count is available for that predecessor. The Grok 4 Fast original announcement says it uses learnings from Grok 4 and is smaller/faster, defeating an unchanged flagship-size assumption. Standard November 17 consumer 4.1, later Grok 4.3 endpoint redirection, and 4.5-to-4.6-to-4.7 generated training trajectories do not establish original Fast model size.
